description_full: REA Group Limited, together with its subsidiaries, engages in digital advertising business in Australia, Asia, and North America. It provides property and property-related services on websites and mobile applications. The company operates residential, commercial, and share property sites, such as realestate.com.au, realcommercial.com.au, Flatmates.com.au, property.com.au, housing.com, and realtor.com. It is also involved in the provision of mortgage brokerage and home financing solutions; property data services; mortgage application and e-lodgement solutions for the broking and lending industries; commercial real estate information and technology; vendor paid advertising; digital non-bank lending solutions; and home loans. The company was formerly known as realestate.com.au Ltd. and changed its name to REA Group Limited in December 2008. The company was incorporated in 1995 and is headquartered in Richmond, Australia. REA Group Limited operates as a subsidiary of News Australia Pty Limited.

financial_summary: REA Group Ltd is a large-cap communication services business with a $16.3B market cap on $1.4B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +13% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +3.2pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 31% against a 7% cost of capital — a 24-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 99% confirm genuine pricing power.
The business throws off $427M in free cash flow — roughly 31 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 2.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 63% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.4× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
